<summary>
Turns 1-2: Agent explored /home/travis/build/failed and identified repo at /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto with modules common, factory, service, util, value, plus pom.xml and build-pom.xml (symlink build.pom.xml -> build-pom.xml). Some find/ls commands contained typos in the printed command string but repository listing succeeded.

Turn 3: Running “mvn -e test” at repo root (using default pom.xml) succeeded.

Turn 4: Inspected .travis.yml. Travis runs:
- install: mvn -B -U -f build.pom.xml dependency:go-offline test clean --quiet --fail-never -DskipTests=true
- script: mvn -B -U -f build-pom.xml verify --fail-at-end -Dsource.skip=true -Dmaven.javadoc.skip=true
(JDKs listed are oraclejdk7/openjdk7, but local environment differs.)

Turn 5: Ran the Travis “verify” command (using build-pom.xml). Build failed during dependency resolution for modules auto-common, auto-factory, auto-service with:
“Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar”
AutoValue module got skipped due to earlier failures.

Turn 6: Searched for tools.jar / com.sun:tools; only hits were in root pom.xml around lines ~178/184.

Turn 7: Viewed root pom.xml profiles section: profiles activate based on presence of ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar (default-profile) or ${java.home}/../Classes/classes.jar (mac-profile), setting a “toolsjar” property accordingly.

Turn 8: Viewed build-pom.xml: it is a simple aggregator POM (build-only) listing modules: ., common, factory, service, value and distributionManagement pointing to a local fake repo.

Turn 9-10: Grepped module poms for com.sun/tools.jar/systemPath; no matches besides root pom.xml. Opened common/pom.xml showing it inherits from com.google.auto:auto-parent version 3 and declares normal deps (guava, test deps).

Turn 11: Viewed the top of root pom.xml: auto-parent version is 4-SNAPSHOT; sets java.version=1.6 and compiler plugin settings.

Turn 12: Checked environment: Java 11.0.27 and Maven 3.6.3 are used locally, explaining why tools.jar (removed since JDK9) is missing.

Turn 13: Opened ~/.m2/repository/com/google/auto/auto-parent/3/auto-parent-3.pom; it contains the same tools.jar-based profile setting “toolsjar” but no further investigation of where com.sun:tools system-scoped dependency is coming from yet.

Turns 14-15: Additional greps for toolsjar/systemPath/com.sun across modules returned no matches (also included minor grep typos in the printed command strings).
</summary>
